title: Microsoft Azure
supports: Blue Yonder applications run on Microsoft Azure infrastructure.

title: What is the Blue Yonder Platform?
supports: Blue Yonder Platform Data Cloud is built on Snowflake and acts as a shared data lakehouse.

title: Blue Yonder named a leader in the 2026 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Warehouse Management Systems
supports: Blue Yonder Warehouse Management is delivered on a cloud-native architecture built on Microsoft Azure. | The WMS uses Blue Yonder Platform capabilities for data, analytics, AI and orchestration.

title: Consafe Logistics
supports: Consafe positions Astro WMS and Astro Go WMS as products built on modern technology platforms. | Public product material confirms SaaS/cloud positioning but does not expose implementation language or database engine.

title: What WMS Capabilities Do You Need - Checklist
supports: Deposco describes its WMS platform as cloud-native on Amazon Web Services. | It describes a singular codebase and singular database with service-based, load-balanced features. | The public source does not identify the database engine.

title: Warehouse Management System LFS
supports: LFS supports Windows, Linux and IBM iSeries platforms. | EPG states that LFS works with Oracle, Microsoft SQL Server and IBM Db2 databases. | Mobile clients include Android and iOS and cloud hosting is available.

title: Frappe / ERPNext Helm Chart
supports: ERPNext has an official Kubernetes Helm deployment. | The chart uses MariaDB and Redis components for ERPNext/Frappe workloads.

title: Frappe Framework
supports: Frappe is a full-stack framework using Python and MariaDB server-side with a JavaScript client library. | Frappe automatically exposes REST APIs and supports Docker-based self-hosting.

title: Warehouse Management System
supports: Current Infor WMS runs on the Infor Industry Cloud Platform.

title: Infor WMS User and Administration Library (Cloud)
supports: Infor WMS cloud documentation exposes Infor OS, ION and API Gateway as technology-platform services.

title: Reports overview
supports: Infor WMS 11.5 documentation describes report scheduling with SQL Server Agent or Oracle Scheduler. | This is historical/product-deployment evidence, not proof of the current SaaS transactional database.

title: Logiwa API Swagger
supports: Logiwa exposes a REST/OpenAPI HTTP API.

title: Logiwa IO
supports: Logiwa IO is positioned as cloud-native, headless and API-first.

title: Technology Overview - Manhattan Active Cloud
supports: ActivePlatform is built around independently scalable microservices. | Containers and Kubernetes are core deployment technologies and microservices are delivered as Docker images.

title: What is Cloud Native?
supports: Manhattan Active solutions are SaaS, powered by Google Cloud, and composed of microservices. | The platform identifies Docker, MySQL and Elastic among its containerized/cloud-native technologies. | Manhattan Active APIs use REST-style resource URLs and JSON.

title: Easy WMS Warehouse Management System
supports: Easy WMS supports cloud and on-premise deployment. | Mecalux describes the cloud version as using a microservices architecture.

title: New Gregoire-Besson distribution centre in France
supports: A documented Easy WMS deployment runs through a Microsoft SQL Server database in a virtualized environment. | This is deployment evidence, not a universal database requirement.

title: Finance and operations application architecture
supports: Dynamics 365 finance and operations applications use Microsoft Azure services including Azure SQL Database and Azure Storage.

title: X++ language reference
supports: X++ is used for ERP and database application programming and compiles to Microsoft .NET CIL.

title: Odoo 19 - Architecture Overview
supports: Odoo uses a three-tier architecture. | Business logic is written in Python, presentation uses HTML5/JavaScript/CSS, and PostgreSQL is the supported RDBMS. | Odoo uses its in-house OWL frontend framework.

title: Odoo 19 - Source install
supports: Odoo 19 requires Python 3.10+ and PostgreSQL 13+.

title: OpenBoxes - Basic Architecture
supports: OpenBoxes documents Grails, Spring, Hibernate and REST API as core technologies. | It documents MySQL and Tomcat among current deployment technologies.

title: OpenBoxes - Database
supports: OpenBoxes supports MySQL 8 as its primary database and MariaDB 10.x as an alternative.

title: OpenBoxes source repository
supports: OpenBoxes source is predominantly Groovy with JavaScript as a significant secondary language. | The project identifies Grails as a core technology.

title: Warehouse Management 26C - RESTful Web Services
supports: Oracle Warehouse Management Cloud exposes RESTful web services.

title: PSI Products
supports: PSI states that modern Java technology forms the common basis for its products.

title: PSIwms
supports: PSIwms provides a web client and supports SaaS, hosted/private/public cloud and on-premise deployment models.

title: ABAP Platform
supports: ABAP Platform is the basis of the SAP S/4HANA product line and is optimized for SAP HANA.

title: Extended Warehouse Management (EWM)
supports: Current SAP EWM is available embedded in SAP S/4HANA or as decentralized EWM based on SAP S/4HANA.

title: SAP Fiori Architecture
supports: SAP Fiori web apps use SAPUI5 and retrieve business data from back-end systems through OData services.

title: WAMAS End User License Agreement
supports: WAMAS licensing materials include Oracle Database special provisions. | This establishes an Oracle Database dependency/use relationship for WAMAS, but not that Oracle is the exclusive or universal primary database.

title: Introducing the Future of Intralogistics Software
supports: SynQ is a modular, cloud-enabled software platform combining warehouse management, material flow, automation control and business intelligence.

title: Tecsys Wins Warehouse Management System of the Year Award
supports: Tecsys WMS is built on the Elite secure SaaS platform. | Tecsys identifies Itopia as a low-code layer and TecsysIQ as an AI intelligence layer.
